title: How the Claude Code team reviews code once agents write most of it
friendlyTitle: How one team reviews code when an agent writes most of it
summary: Anthropic's Claude Code team described its review path on 15 October. It says Claude writes about 90% of that product's code, and that from June to September merged pull requests more than doubled while the share that had to be reverted fell by more than 40%. Most reading now happens before a person looks: tests, a fresh-context agent review, required CI, a second agent vote on findings, and a security pass. A classifier then asks for no person, one, or two, and some paths always need a person.
friendlySummary: The Claude Code team says an agent writes about 90% of its own code. From June to September, merged changes more than doubled, and fewer of them had to be undone. Machines check most changes first. A person still has to approve riskier ones.
whyItMatters: Teams letting agents open pull requests can copy the split: automate the routine checks, keep a person on auth, billing and release paths, and watch revert rates so saved review time does not come back as incidents. The public reviewer posts findings, not approvals, and is on Team and Enterprise plans.
friendlyWhyItMatters: If agents open changes for you, let machines catch routine mistakes and keep a person on anything that can break payments, logins or releases. Watch how often changes have to be undone.
